1.title: Benefits of Cloud Services
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Benefits of Cloud Services. It covers the exam area Describe cloud concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud. Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud. Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud. Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe cloud concepts (twenty-five to thirty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The benefits at a glance
1.text: The benefits at a glance. High availability. One-line meaning: The service keeps running when parts fail. Key words in a question: uptime, S L A (service level agreement), failure, zones. Scalability. One-line meaning: Add or remove capacity to match demand. Key words in a question: peak, growth, demand. Reliability. One-line meaning: The system recovers from failure and keeps working. Key words in a question: resilient, self-healing, disaster recovery.

1.title: The benefits at a glance, continued
1.text: The benefits at a glance. Predictability. One-line meaning: Performance and cost can be foreseen. Key words in a question: forecast, consistent, budget. Security. One-line meaning: Built-in protection and compliance support. Key words in a question: threats, encryption, compliance. Governance. One-line meaning: Rules and standards applied to resources. Key words in a question: policy, standards, control. Manageability. One-line meaning: Easy to manage and monitor the resources. Key words in a question: automation, templates, portal.

1.title: The benefits at a glance, continued
1.text: The benefits at a glance. The figure shows this: The seven cloud benefits grouped by the four study guide skills.

1.title: High availability and scalability
1.text: High availability and scalability. High availability means the service is up when users need it. In the cloud you design with several copies of a resource in different places so one failure does not stop the service. Providers state targets in a service level agreement, for example ninety-nine point nine percent or ninety-nine point nine nine percent uptime. for current numbers. Scalability means you can change capacity to match demand.

1.title: High availability and scalability, continued
1.text: High availability and scalability. Vertical scaling (scale up). What it does: Make one resource bigger (more C P U or memory). Example: Move a V M to a larger size. Horizontal scaling (scale out). What it does: Add more copies of the resource. Example: Add more V M instances behind a load balancer. Autoscaling. What it does: Scale automatically by rules or schedule. Example: Add instances when C P U is high. Exam tip: Scale up or down equals bigger or smaller machine. Scale out or in equals more or fewer machines. Elasticity (growing and shrinking automatically with demand) is why you pay only for what you need.

1.title: Reliability and predictability
1.text: Reliability and predictability. Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from failures and keep functioning. In Azure it is supported by. Decentralized design: resources can be placed across datacenters, zones and regions (Module four). Backup and disaster recovery services. Global footprint: a regional problem does not take down every region. Predictability has two sides.

1.title: Reliability and predictability, continued
1.text: Reliability and predictability. Performance predictability. Meaning: The app behaves consistently as demand changes. Tools: autoscaling, load balancing. Cost predictability. Meaning: You can forecast and control spending. Tools: pricing calculator, cost analysis, budgets (Module eleven). Exam tip: Reliability equals recover from failure; high availability equals stay up. If the question says "recover" or "disaster", think reliability; if it says "uptime" or "S L A", think high availability.

1.title: Security and governance
1.text: Security and governance. Security. The cloud provider secures the physical infrastructure, and the platform offers tools for you to secure your own part (identity, network controls, encryption, threat protection). The shared responsibility model (Module one) decides who does what. Governance. Cloud governance means applying rules and standards to resources: which regions and sizes are allowed, which tags are required, how access is granted. Azure helps with Azure Policy, resource locks, role-based access control and Microsoft Purview (Modules nine and twelve). Compliance. Azure supports many compliance standards and has audit reports. The provider's certification does not make your own workload compliant: you must still configure it correctly. Exam tip: A common trap: "The provider is compliant, so my app is compliant." Wrong: compliance is shared.

1.title: Manageability
1.text: Manageability. Manageability has two parts in the study guide. Management of the cloud. Meaning: Autoscaling, monitoring and alerts, templates and automation for the resources you run. Examples: Azure Monitor, autoscale, A R M (Azure Resource Manager) templates. Management in the cloud. Meaning: The ways you reach and administer resources. Examples: Azure portal, C L I, Power Shell, R E S T (representational state transfer) A P Is. Because resources are defined as code and managed through a common interface, you can deploy the same environment again and again with little manual work.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A web shop must handle a short rush of orders on one day, then return to normal. Which benefit lets it add capacity and release it afterward? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Scalability and elasticity. Scalability, together with elasticity, allows capacity to grow and shrink with demand.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team adds three more identical virtual machines behind a load balancer. What kind of scaling is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Horizontal scaling (scale out). Adding more instances is scaling out (horizontal). Scaling up makes one machine larger.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An application keeps running when one datacenter in a region fails because copies run elsewhere. Which cloud benefit is shown? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: High availability. High availability keeps the service running when part of the infrastructure fails.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A finance team wants to forecast monthly cloud spending and receive alerts when a budget is near. Which benefit is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Predictability (cost). Cost predictability uses estimating and budgeting tools to forecast and control spending.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company enforces that every resource must be created only in approved regions. Which benefit is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Governance. Governance applies rules and standards, for example with Azure Policy.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An administrator deploys the same environment in three regions using a template. Which benefit is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Manageability. Templates and automation make resources easy to deploy and manage the same way every time.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does an S L A state? Answer: The uptime or performance target the provider commits to for a service. Question two. Scale up or scale out: which adds more instances? Answer: Scale out (horizontal). Question three. Which benefit lets the system recover from failure and keep working? Answer: Reliability.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the two sides of predictability. Answer: Performance predictability and cost predictability. Question five. What is governance in the cloud? Answer: Applying rules and standards to resources, for example with Azure Policy. Question six. Is a provider's compliance certificate enough to make your workload compliant? Answer: No. Compliance is shared; you must configure your part correctly.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. High availability: stays up through failures; stated by an S L A. Scalability: scale up or down equals bigger or smaller; scale out or in equals more or fewer; autoscale by rules. Reliability: recovers from failure; decentralized design, backup, disaster recovery. Predictability: performance (autoscale, load balance) and cost (calculator, budgets). Security: provider secures the infrastructure; you secure identities, data, configuration. Governance: rules and standards: Azure Policy, locks, R B A C, Purview. Manageability: management of the cloud (autoscale, monitoring, templates) and in the cloud (portal, C L I, Power Shell, A P Is). In the next module, we continue the course.
